In the beginning, the world was silent. The mountains stood tall, the rivers flowed, and the wind moved through empty valleys, but there was no sound—only endless quiet.

A young spirit named Aria wandered this soundless realm, lonely and longing for connection. One day, she climbed the highest peak and opened her mouth, releasing the first cry ever heard. It rang out pure and clear, shattering the ancient silence.

But the cry did not fade. Instead, it struck the mountain wall and returned to her—transformed, softer, yet unmistakably her own voice. Startled, Aria called out again. Again, the mountain answered.

She laughed, and laughter came back. She sang, and songs multiplied through the valleys.

The mountain explained: "I am giving back what you have given me, but I cannot create sound myself. I can only return what I receive."

Aria understood. She traveled the world, teaching others to speak, sing, and shout. And wherever they went, the cliffs and caves would answer, returning their voices as echoes.

This is why echoes exist—they are the world's way of giving back what we offer, reminding us that what we send out into the world often returns to us, transformed but recognizable.

"Grant me darkness," Mira pleaded, "so I may have something of my own."

The Moon, moved by her courage, whispered a secret: "Stand before your sister the Sun, and I will give you the first shadow."

When Mira descended, she positioned herself before the Sun Goddess. The Moon, though hidden, bent a tiny portion of light around Mira's form. For the first time, darkness appeared—a silhouette stretching behind her.

The Sun Goddess gasped, then smiled. "You have created something beautiful," she said. "A space that is yours alone."

From that day forward, all things cast shadows. And humanity learned that even in a world of light, everyone deserves a place of their own darkness—a mystery that belongs only to them.
